newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit snowed under by dollar rise.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit snowed under by dollar rise.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit dropped through the key 2.5000 resistance level against the dollar on Thursday following the U.S. unit's sharp overnight gains against the majors.
"It started with some stop-loss sales caused by the dollar. Then there was a big ringgit sale by a Hong Kong party," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.
An assistant chief dealer with a European bank said the dollar could extend its gains to 2.5080 ringgit, if the breach of 2.5050 proved to be a firm break.
Dealers said the dollar should stay supported around 2.5030 on commercial demand ahead of the month-end and the Japanese half-year end.
A Kuala Lumpur-based British bank dealer said the market was buying dollars on every dip as month-end demand from Kuala Lumpur was still to be met.
The ringgit was quoted at 2.5050/55 at 0430 GMT, after reaching a high of 2.5055 against 2.5013/20 at the close of Kuala Lumpur trading on Wednesday.

In Indonesia, the rupiah held steady as players focused on month-end liquidity while keeping an eye on possible developments in a court hearing involving ousted opposition leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
Jakarta dealers said operators' concern about Friday's expected liquidity conditions was reflected by rises in tom/next swap rate. It rose to 2.8 points from 1.6 points at the opening.
A U.S. bank dealer said worries over possible unrest in connection with the court hearing kept operators from unloading the dollar aggressively despite liquidity concerns.
An Indonesian judge postponed a ruling on Megawati's lawsuit shortly before noon after the defence questioned his jurisdiction.

Megawati, the daughter of Indonesia's founding president Sukarno, has launched a court case against the government for backing rebels in the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), who ousted her from the party leadership in June.
Her sacking led to an unusual wave of dissent against the government, culminating in a police raid on PDI headquarters in July which triggered Jakarta's worst riots in more than two decades.

Elsewhere, the Singapore dollar remained relatively firm as talk of large U.S. dollar sell orders by the Brunei Investment Agency around S$1.4110 and long U.S. dollar positions kept dollar/Sing from rising.
"Brunei exports a lot of oil and they're paid in dollars. There's no market for their currency so they're looking to sell through dollar/Sing," said the European bank dealer.
Dealers said talk of the Brunei sell orders had kept the U.S. dollar from appreciating above the S$1.4100 level in recent weeks.

"A lot of people are happy to sell dollar/Sing at 1.4090/95. Major players are already long on dollar/Sing so that limits the U.S. dollar's ability to move much higher," said Andy Tan, economist and general manager at MMS International.
The Thai baht slid to 25.394-25.397 at midday against 25.360-25.265 late on Wednesday in line with the dollar's rise against the majors.
But dealers in Bangkok said the baht's decline was inhibited by some profit-taking on the dollar.
